To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

institutions can have an important influence on cultural diversity and that bottom up processes such as referenda tend to produce cultural convergence, while top down processes such as propaganda tend to produce cultural diversity.

(1) institutions can have a positive impact on cultural diversity, (2) democratic processes tend to produce cultural convergence, (3) propaganda can increase diversity when it is the only form of institutional influence, but when democratic processes are frequent, they can reverse or neutralize the effects of propaganda, (4) our models allow for a full spectrum of diversity control, and (5) our results have implications for political and sociological theory and practice.
(i) institutions can have a positive impact on cultural diversity and (ii) bottom up processes such as referenda can counteract the positive impact of top down processes such as propaganda.
